parsed.explanation: Thin, encyclopaedic dossier. Same-sex conduct is legal and no trans-specific criminal offence, police targeting, violence or custody practice is documented. But there is no gender-identity recognition or document remedy, so an outable visitor carries passport/presentation mismatch into border, immigration and hotel checks with the law silent and no recourse. Anti-discrimination and hate-crime grounds are sexual-orientation-only, not gender identity. Social evidence is general LGBTQ stigma, with no trans-specific acceptance or hostility finding. Absence of incidents reflects no monitoring, not safety. The combined regime is less active than explicit border-denial or police-stop anchors but lacks the working remedies of higher anchors. Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender-identity recognition or marker-change procedure; passport/presentation mismatch is visible at every border, immigration and hotel document check; law and policy are silent on handling; no domestic remedy.
entry_documents.protection: None documented. UN joint statement creates no domestic mechanism; no consular or bilateral arrangement on mismatch.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch may trigger questioning or secondary inspection, but no denial, arrest or removal is documented; hotel staff exposure is also unresolved.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented trans-specific arrest, detention, interrogation or custody-placement practice. If a document discrepancy escalates, no protocol is documented.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No documented safeguard, legal-aid route or custody rule for trans travellers.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Unknown; dossier records no enforcement action or police practice bearing on trans people.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No subnational variation or facility-access rule documented; no evidence of bathroom, ward or custody restrictions reaching visitors.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: No documented interaction between national and local regimes; town/country difference is expectation only.

care_services.exposure: No general anti-discrimination protection beyond employment; gender identity is not named in the labour code or hate-crime provision, so no GI-inclusive recourse in healthcare, housing or services. No documented denial of care to trans visitors.
care_services.protection: None GI-specific; sexual-orientation-only employment and sentencing grounds may not fit.
care_services.interaction: Hospital or emergency exposure via document mismatch is possible but undocumented; no remedy shown.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No trans-specific criminalisation or state threat-framing documented; same-sex conduct is legal. General LGBTQ stigmatisation is described, not trans-specific.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Sexual-orientation hate-crime enhancement only; no gender-identity-named hate crime or protection machinery. UN statement has no enforcement.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Police response to anti-trans incidents is undocumented; the sexual-orientation ground may not cover a trans victim.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific trans rule documented. A trans minor travelling with a guardian faces the same unaddressed document-mismatch exposure; age-of-consent discrepancy is not trans-specific.
minors_guardians.protection: None documented for trans minors or guardians.
minors_guardians.interaction: Unknown; no school, facility, custody or border practice involving minors is recorded.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence or police response documented; absence reflects no monitoring/reporting, not safety. General LGBTQ stigma only.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No gender-identity hate-crime recourse; sexual-orientation-only enhancement. No victim-support or police-protection outcome recorded.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If violence occurs, whether police treat it as anti-trans or fit it to a sexual-orientation ground is unknown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No domestic document remedy, no general anti-discrimination, no gender-identity hate crime; UN signature creates no complaint body. Visitor must rely on a sexual-orientation ground or none.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Complaints about border, hotel treatment or violence have no documented route; outcomes are unknown.

anchor_checks.comparison: Vellandra documents an active border register denying entry and routine discretionary refusals. This dossier has no denial rule or enforcement action, only unaddressed document mismatch. It is less exposed than 0.35-A, though it lacks even that hostile procedure's clarity.

Kestrel Isles documents extended secondary screening, discretionary refused admission and an appeal desk. This dossier records no such border practice, no appeal route and no remedy. It sits lower on active enforcement but similar in unresolved document-check uncertainty.

Meridia has trained border officers, tribunal appeals, release and compensation. This dossier has no gender-identity recognition, no operative remedy and no documented protection outcome. It is clearly below 0.75-C.

Vesskar has a public-order statute penalising deceptive presentation and documented detention/humiliation, plus a narrow discrimination claim. This dossier has no such statute or documented detention, but also no anti-discrimination remedy. It is roughly comparable or slightly safer on active enforcement.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime is legally non-criminalising but institutionally silent on gender identity. The main traveller-facing exposure is documentary: no marker remedy means mismatch can surface at every border, immigration and hotel check, with no stated protocol and no domestic recourse. Protections exist only for sexual orientation in employment and hate-crime sentencing, not gender identity, and the UN statement is non-operative. Social evidence is thin and general LGBTQ stigma, not a documented trans-specific threat. No trans-specific violence, arrest or custody practice is documented, but that is absence of monitoring. Net: Elevated Risk, below regimes with functioning remedies and above active border-denial or police-stop regimes.
